transcript.text: Excellent. This is exactly why we run this checkpoint. Let me synthesize what I'm hearing and propose how we proceed. We have three interlocking issues: First, from Tom, our university license restricts exclusivity to industrial analytics only — healthcare and other fields must remain available to us. Second, from Nia, component U-7 is university-owned and not within our sublicense rights, so it must be carved out of the license entirely, and any deployment involving U-7 needs written university consent. That lab-record confirmation should be added to the transaction checklist immediately. Third, from Marcus, Meridian requires sublicensing rights specifically to Orion Industrial, and Meridian accepts that we retain ownership and use of all background technology and improvements. Now, one concern I want to flag: the current draft grants Meridian rights in improvements developed during the license term — that's broad. Given Meridian's own stated position that we retain ownership and use of improvements, we should align the draft to reflect that our company retains ownership of improvements, and Meridian receives only a license to use them, not ownership. I'd like Tom to circulate the 2018 amendment language in the markup thread today, Nia to add the U-7 exclusion and lab-record confirmation to the checklist and flag any consent timelines with the university, and Marcus to confirm with Meridian's counsel that the field-of-use limitation and U-7 carve-out are acceptable before we revise the term sheet. If we can get those confirmations and redline revisions by midweek, we should still be on track for signing next week.
